source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.teacher_note: doubling still holds here even though For doubled numbers, compare prime factors before and after doubling to see the extra 2 is missing from the stem — on the item about When both numbers are multiplied by the same factor, is.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is doubling because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'When both numbers are multiplied by the same factor, is that shared' as the operative test.

intelligence.enrichment: Doubling both numbers adds an extra factor of 2 to both prime factorisations, so the HCF doubles; a visible common multiplier is a common factor, but shared factors in the remaining multipliers can make the HCF larger than that visible multiplier.
